title: Niko and the Wiggling Cushion
markdown:
Niko the camel loved his cozy library. His favourite spot was a big squishy armchair by the sunny window, topped with a plump cushion. But every afternoon the cushion would wiggle. A little nudge left. A little nudge right.

“Oh my,” Niko would sigh, and scoot it back.

One sunny morning the cushion had wiggled all the way to a tall book tower. Niko wiggled his nose. He wanted to read about brave knights.

“Aha,” he declared. “I’ll be a detective.”

Whoosh. Aunt Olive the owl arrived, peering through sparkly glasses.

“Detectives?” she hooted.

Niko told her about the wiggling cushion. Aunt Olive smiled. “A mystery. How exciting.” She gave Niko a shiny magnifying glass and a teeny detective hat. The hat tickled his ears.

He held up the glass. Everything looked huge.

His first suspect was Lottie the duckling. “Halt. Have you seen my cushion?”

Lottie gave a bubbly quack. “Oh, Niko. Your cushion looked so warm. I nudged it closer to the sunshine so I could watch the dragonflies.” She pointed a webbed foot. “It’s right over there.”

Niko looked. His cushion was basking in the warmest spot. He smelled sweet sunshine and sleepy lavender.

“Thank you, Lottie.”

As he settled down, a gentle whoosh of air swept through the window. The cushion slid again.

“Goodness gracious me,” Niko whispered. The breeze only wanted to give him cool air.

Then Aunt Olive landed nearby. “Niko, dear. Your cushion looks a teeny bit crooked. May I tidy it?” With a soft wing-nudge, she straightened it.

Niko blinked. The sunshine wanted to warm him. The wind wanted to cool him. Aunt Olive wanted to make things neat. These were nice reasons, but not a thrilling mystery. His ears drooped.

“It wasn’t a very exciting mystery,” he mumbled.

Aunt Olive gave him a warm feathery hug. “The best mysteries have kind, helpful answers. Your cushion moved to make everyone happy. And while sunshine is wonderful, it’s nice to have space for your books too.”

Niko looked at his cushion, then at Aunt Olive. Lottie peeked in, eyes bright. A giggly idea popped into his head.

“We can all share. Lottie, you get the sunny spot. I can read from right here. Aunt Olive, you can perch and tell us stories.”

Lottie quacked with delight. Aunt Olive hooted her happy agreement. Soon all three friends were snuggled on the big soft cushion. Niko opened his book. Lottie watched dragonflies. Aunt Olive began a tale that made them giggle.

The cushion was perfect for everyone — a cozy reading spot, a warm sunshine spot, and the best spot for sitting close. Niko turned a page about knights, and the cushion, for a little while, stayed still.
characters: Niko (a library-armchair camel), Lottie (a sunshine duckling), Aunt Olive (a sparkly-glasses owl)
author: StoryGen Community
